strings.d1.s0.name: Dubai Mall
strings.d1.s0.tips: The world's largest mall, with an aquarium window and an ice rink. An air-conditioned start.
strings.d1.s1.name: Dubai Aquarium & Underwater Zoo
strings.d1.s1.tips: A tunnel aquarium inside the mall; watch the sharks.
strings.d1.s2.name: Social House Dubai Mall
strings.d1.s2.tips: International menu with fountain views; lunch.
strings.d1.s3.name: Burj Khalifa At the Top
strings.d1.s3.tips: Floors 124-125; sunset slot (~219 AED). Book tickets online weeks ahead. You get the sunset and the city lights in one visit.
strings.d1.s4.name: Dubai Fountain
strings.d1.s4.tips: The fountain show on Burj Lake runs every 30 minutes; watch it free from the Souk Al Bahar terrace.
strings.d1.b0.name: Time Out Market Dubai
strings.d1.b0.tips: A food market in Souk Al Bahar; lunch with plenty of choice.
strings.d1.b1.name: Sky Views Observatory
strings.d1.b1.tips: A glass walkway facing the Burj; a fallback if Burj tickets are sold out.
strings.d2.theme: Old Dubai: Al Fahidi, abra and souks
strings.d2.s0.name: Al Fahidi Historical Neighbourhood
strings.d2.s0.tips: Stone houses with wind towers; have breakfast at Arabian Tea House and stop by the coffee museum. Cool in the morning.
strings.d2.s1.name: Dubai Museum Al Shindagha
strings.d2.s1.tips: Pearl-diving history and a Creek museum in Shindagha; air-conditioned.
strings.d2.s2.name: Dubai Creek Abra
strings.d2.s2.tips: Cross to Deira by wooden boat for 1 AED; Dubai's cheapest and loveliest moment.
strings.d2.s3.name: Deira Spice Souk
strings.d2.s3.tips: Spices, saffron and incense; haggling is a must, and half the asking price is normal.
strings.d2.s4.name: Al Ustad Special Kabab
strings.d2.s4.tips: Iranian kebabs since 1978; in Bur Dubai, with walls full of photos. Dubai's most famous budget restaurant.
strings.d2.b0.name: Arabian Tea House Al Fahidi
strings.d2.b0.tips: Emirati breakfast or lunch in a courtyard.
strings.d2.b1.name: Deira Gold Souk
strings.d2.b1.tips: The gold market; a window-shopping stroll next to the Spice Souk.
strings.d3.s0.name: Kite Beach
strings.d3.s0.tips: A free sandy beach with views of the Burj Al Arab. Sunbeds cost 50-100 AED, and the sea is 22°C in winter.
strings.d3.s1.name: Jumeirah Mosque
strings.d3.s1.tips: The only mosque tour open to non-Muslims (10:00 and 14:00, SMCCU); architecture and a Q&A.
strings.d3.s2.name: Al Fanar Restaurant Jumeirah
strings.d3.s2.tips: A 1960s-themed Emirati restaurant; try the machboos (spiced rice with meat) and luqaimat (sweet dumplings).
strings.d3.s3.name: Madinat Jumeirah Souk
strings.d3.s3.tips: A man-made souk with canals; the abra ride costs 100 AED, with a sunset view of the Burj Al Arab.
strings.d3.s4.name: Burj Al Arab Viewpoint
strings.d3.s4.tips: Sunset views of the Burj Al Arab from Jumeirah Beach; free.
strings.d3.b0.name: Pierchic Madinat
strings.d3.b0.tips: A restaurant on a pier over the sea; a special evening.
strings.d3.b1.name: Etihad Museum
strings.d3.b1.tips: The museum of the UAE's founding; air-conditioned.
strings.d4.s0.name: Dubai Marina Walk
strings.d4.s0.tips: A marina promenade among the skyscrapers; coffee.
strings.d4.s1.name: The View at The Palm
strings.d4.s1.tips: An observation deck on the 52nd floor of Palm Jumeirah; this is where you see the palm shape.
strings.d4.s2.name: Nakheel Mall
strings.d4.s2.tips: The Palm's mall; an air-conditioned break.
strings.d4.s3.name: Bu Qtair Jumeirah
strings.d4.s3.tips: A fishermen's shack turned legend; fried fish of the day, eaten standing or on a stool.
strings.d4.s4.name: JBR The Walk & Beach
strings.d4.s4.tips: The JBR seafront strip; swim in winter, take an evening stroll in summer, with views of Ain Dubai.
strings.d4.b0.name: Marina Social Dubai
strings.d4.b0.tips: A modern menu in the Marina.
strings.d4.b1.name: Ain Dubai
strings.d4.b1.tips: The world's largest observation wheel; if it is open.
strings.d5.s0.name: Dubai Miracle Garden
strings.d5.s0.tips: A garden of 150 million flowers (open November to April); cool in the morning.
strings.d5.s1.name: Global Village
strings.d5.s1.tips: Country pavilions and street food (October to April).
strings.d5.s2.name: Ravi Restaurant Satwa
strings.d5.s2.tips: Pakistani cuisine; Dubai's most famous budget restaurant. The dal and chicken karahi are good.
strings.d5.s3.name: Lahbab Desert Safari
strings.d5.s3.tips: 4x4 dune bashing over red dunes, camels, sunset, a BBQ and a show; hotel pickup included, 250-400 AED.
strings.d5.b0.name: Al Mallah Satwa
strings.d5.b0.tips: Lebanese shawarma and fruit cocktails; an alternative to Ravi.
strings.d5.b1.name: Al Qudra Lakes
strings.d5.b1.tips: Artificial lakes and flamingos in the desert; go by car instead of the safari.
strings.d6.s0.name: Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque
strings.d6.s0.tips: 1.5 hours from Dubai (E100 bus, 25 AED). It holds the world's largest carpet and chandeliers; entry is free, online registration is required, and an abaya is provided at the entrance.
strings.d6.s1.name: Louvre Abu Dhabi
strings.d6.s1.tips: Jean Nouvel's rain-of-light dome; on Saadiyat Island, air-conditioned.
strings.d6.s2.name: Louvre Abu Dhabi Cafe
strings.d6.s2.tips: Lunch at the museum cafe, beneath the dome.
strings.d6.s3.name: Qasr Al Watan
strings.d6.s3.tips: The presidential palace; white marble and a library.
strings.d6.s4.name: Abu Dhabi Corniche
strings.d6.s4.tips: A seafront promenade; the return bus leaves at 18:30.
strings.d6.b0.name: Emirates Palace Le Café
strings.d6.b0.tips: Gold-flecked cappuccino in the palace hotel.
strings.d6.b1.name: Ferrari World Yas Island
strings.d6.b1.tips: The world's fastest roller coaster; an alternative to the palace.
strings.d7.s0.name: Alserkal Avenue
strings.d7.s0.tips: An art gallery district in Al Quoz; coffee and free exhibitions.
strings.d7.s1.name: Karama Market
strings.d7.s2.name: Logma Boxpark
strings.d7.s2.tips: A modern Emirati cafe; regag bread (thin Emirati flatbread) and karak tea, a farewell.
strings.d7.s3.name: Dubai Metro Red Line Airport
strings.d7.s3.tips: Take the metro to DXB Terminals 1-3; goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: Karak House Jumeirah
strings.d7.b0.tips: Karak tea and Emirati breakfast; a light farewell.
strings.d7.b1.name: Jameel Arts Centre
strings.d7.b1.tips: Contemporary art on the Creek; an alternative to Alserkal.
strings.note0: Use the metro with a Nol card (Red Line from the airport to the Marina); taxis are cheap and reliable (Careem/Uber). The E100 bus to Abu Dhabi costs 25 AED.
strings.note1: November to March is ideal at 20-28°C, good for the beach, the desert and being outdoors. Evenings are cool, so bring a cardigan.
strings.note2: Mosque visits require long sleeves and a headscarf; an abaya is provided at Sheikh Zayed. Alcohol is served only in licensed hotels and restaurants.
strings.note3: Burj Khalifa sunset tickets sell out weeks ahead, as do Museum of the Future tickets.
strings.note4: Old Dubai is cheap and authentic: an abra costs 1 AED and a kebab at Al Ustad 60 AED; Downtown and the Marina are expensive.
strings.note5: A 10% tip is common; haggling in the souks is a must, so start at half the price.
strings.transit.name: Nol Card
strings.transit.why_chosen: Valid on the metro, tram, buses and abra; the Silver card is the most practical.
